Source of Applicants (extended: UTM tracker URL)
Website (extended: jobs search provider + suggested controller)

behavioral_notes.observation: The public jobs listing runs website._search_with_fuzzy('jobs', ...) to fuzzy-match job names/descriptions, then filters in Python by department_id, address_id (office), res.country, hr.contract.type and res.partner.industry (plus is_remote/is_other_department/is_untyped/is_industry_untyped 'unset' buckets). It contaminates the result set per filter to compute live facet counters (count_per_office/department/employment_type/industry/country) so each filter shows its remaining count, geo-detects the visitor country via request.geoip.country_code to pre-filter, then paginates 12 jobs/page via website.pager. This routing/filtering logic is invisible in Python field metadata.

The /jobs/apply/<job> page renders a website.form posting to /website/form/ with data-model_name='hr.applicant' and a hidden data-for='hr_recruitment_form' carrying job_id/department_id. On POST, WebsiteForm creates an hr.applicant: HrApplicant.website_form_input_filter checks the hr.job is still active (raises UserError 'The job offer has been closed.' otherwise) and stamps stage_id to the first non-folded recruitment stage for that job; extract_data relabels the free-text 'short_introduction'. The uploaded resume becomes an ir.attachment on the applicant. config_data.xml whitelists the postable fields (email_from, partner_name, partner_phone, job_id, department_id, linkedin_profile, applicant_properties) via formbuilder_whitelist and sets website_form_key='apply_job'. This anonymous public record creation is the module's core side-effect, driven by Python, not schema.

hr.job._inherit adds website.published.multi.mixin; website_published (tracked) is the public-visibility gate. _onchange_website_published mirrors website_published into is_published, set_open() and action_archive() force website_published=False, and _compute_published_date stamps published_date=today on publish. Four ir.rule record rules enforce that base.group_public and base.group_portal can only read hr.job where website_published=True (hr_recruitment.group_hr_recruitment_user sees all); a parallel rule exposes hr.department only when it has a published job or children. _search_get_detail re-asserts ('website_published','=',True) when a sudo() country search bypasses the rule. Visibility semantics live in code/data, not metadata.

A public jsonrpc endpoint called on form focus-out (by the hr_recruitment_form interaction) de-duplicates candidates before submit: it searches hr.applicant.sudo() by normalized email / partner_name / partner_phone / linkedin_profile scoped to the job's website, groups by application_status, and returns a human-readable warning if an ongoing application exists or a refused one was created within the last 6 months (relativedelta(months=6)), optionally surfacing the recruiter's contact. Anti-duplicate UX logic invisible in field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.job detail template — Google for Jobs structured data (SEO/og)
behavioral_notes.observation: The /jobs/<job> detail view inherits website.seo.metadata (so SEO/og tags are editable per job) and emits JobPosting microdata: itemprop employmentType (from hr.contract.type), datePosted (published_date), title, directApply=true, hiringOrganization name + /logo.png, jobLocation address (res.partner.contact_address) or jobLocationType=TELECOMMUTE for remote. full_url is computed by joining the base URL with website_url (/jobs/<slug>) for sharing. This SEO surface is template/code-level, not Python metadata.

7 JS files; 1 OWL component (CopyClipboardCharField); the public apply page is driven by the public.interaction 'website_hr_recruitment.hr_recruitment_form' (live LinkedIn-URL regex validation + RPC duplicate warnings + conditional resume/linkedin requirement); registry adds fields:CopyClipboardJobLinkButton + fields:boolean_toggle_labeled and website.form_editor_actions:apply_job (so the builder can drop the Apply form); patches NewContentSystrayItem.prototype (New > Job Position). Asset bundles {web.assets_frontend:2, web.assets_backend:3, website.website_builder_assets:2, website.assets_editor:1, web.assets_tests:1}.

classification.rationale: website_hr_recruitment is a value-network mediation layer (Stabell & Fjeldstad): it operates a website storefront/portal that publishes the employer brand and connects two parties — job seekers and the recruiting organization — over a shared infrastructure (the careers site, SEO/Google-for-Jobs exposure, and the apply channel). Its routes are public web/portal surfaces (/jobs listing + search, /jobs/<job> detail, /jobs/apply submission) rather than a transform document-flow (chain) or a problem-solving engagement (shop), the signature of the 'network' configuration shared by website/portal modules. It is a primary activity because it is the front-facing acquisition channel that directly captures candidates (creating hr.applicant), the inbound edge of the talent-acquisition stream — not a behind-the-scenes support function. It maps to APQC PCF 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital, specifically 7.1 'Recruit, source and select employees' (the online sourcing/application channel). The terminal output is an hr.applicant handed to hr_recruitment's source-to-hire pipeline; no flow to stock/account. Note: the parent module hr_recruitment is classed 'support'; this website channel is the candidate-facing network/primary storefront layered on top of it.

fuzzy site search over job name/description with facet counters
filter jobs by country, department, office (address), contract type and industry, plus remote/untyped buckets
geo-IP country pre-filtering of the job list
publish/unpublish a job via website_published with public/portal ir.rule gating
drag-and-drop Apply form (website builder) creating hr.applicant from anonymous visitors
resume/CV upload as ir.attachment + LinkedIn URL validation
Google for Jobs JobPosting structured data + per-job SEO/og metadata
UTM-tracked recruitment source URLs for channel attribution
typical_fits: standard published-jobs board with department/office/contract filtering
anonymous online application creating an applicant in the recruiter pipeline
employer-brand careers pages styled in the website builder
SEO-optimized job postings indexable by Google for Jobs
common_gaps: candidate assessment questionnaires on the public form (hr_recruitment_survey)
candidate self-service portal to track application status post-submit
multi-language / localized job descriptions beyond html_translate defaults
captcha / advanced anti-spam beyond the duplicate-application check
external job-board syndication (LinkedIn/Indeed posting) — only inbound UTM links here
